 28	// summarize the older messages, so a long session stays within the main
 29	// model's context window. It is a close port of aider's ChatSummary — recursive
 30	// split: keep a recent tail, summarize the older head, recurse — run

 33		client llm.ModelClient

 36		out    Output

 41	// are the same ports the coder talks through, so a compaction retry reports
 42	// and sleeps exactly like a turn's.
 43	func NewChatSummary(client llm.ModelClient, side *config.Model, tokens TokenCounter, out Output, clock Clock) *ChatSummary {
 44		return &ChatSummary{client: client, side: side, tokens: tokens, out: out, clock: clock}

 52	// compacting, so the budget that decides when to compact must see it.
 53	func (s *ChatSummary) count(m llm.Message) int {

 99		if depth == 0 && s.total(msgs) <= maxTokens {
100			return msgs, nil
101		}
102		if len(msgs) <= summaryMinSplit || depth > summaryMaxDepth {
103			return s.summarizeAll(msgs)
104		}
105	
106		// Pick a split so the preserved tail sums to under half the budget, then
107		// back up so the summarized head ends on an assistant boundary.
108		half := maxTokens / 2
109		tailTokens := 0
110		split := len(msgs)
111		for i, m := range slices.Backward(msgs) {
112			t := s.count(m)
113			if tailTokens+t >= half {
114				break
115			}
116			tailTokens += t
117			split = i
118		}
119		for split > 1 && msgs[split-1].Role != llm.RoleAssistant {
120			split--
121		}
122		if split <= summaryMinSplit {
123			return s.summarizeAll(msgs)
124		}
125	
126		tail := msgs[split:]
127	
128		// Feed the side model as much of the head as its window allows.
129		bound := s.sideInputBound() - summaryInputBuffer
130		var keep []llm.Message
131		acc := 0
132		for _, m := range msgs[:split] {
133			acc += s.count(m)
134			if acc > bound {
135				break
136			}
137			keep = append(keep, m)
138		}
139	
140		summary, err := s.summarizeAll(keep)
141		if err != nil {
142			return nil, err
143		}
144	
145		combined := make([]llm.Message, 0, len(summary)+len(tail))
146		combined = append(combined, summary...)
147		combined = append(combined, tail...)
148		if s.total(summary)+s.total(tail) < maxTokens {
149			return combined, nil
150		}
151		return s.summarizeReal(combined, maxTokens, depth+1)
152	}

197	// renderForSummary lays the messages out for the side model.
198	//
199	// It used to skip every role that was not USER or ASSISTANT, which in a harness
200	// where everything a turn does arrives as tool calls meant the summarizer saw
201	// only the thin prose layer: a turn that made twelve tool calls and closed with
202	// one sentence compacted to that sentence. The work was invisible to the thing
203	// summarizing the work.
204	//
205	// Three consequences of including the rest:
206	//
207	// Tool *calls* carry the intent — which file, which pattern — so they are shown
208	// in full. Tool *results* carry file contents and search output, which is
209	// exactly what the prompt asks the model to drop, so they are cut to a budget:
210	// enough to see what came back, not enough to pay for it twice.
211	//
212	// No role is skipped, and that is the subtle one: an earlier summary must
213	// survive into a later fold, or compaction erases its own output — worse than
214	// the fold it replaced. That held when the summary was a system message and
215	// holds now that it is a marked user turn; not filtering by role at all is what
216	// makes it robust to the carrier changing again.
217	func renderForSummary(msgs []llm.Message) string {
218		var b strings.Builder
219		for _, m := range msgs {
220			body := strings.TrimRight(m.Text(), "\n")
221			switch m.Role {
222			case llm.RoleTool:
223				body = clipForSummary(body)
224			case llm.RoleAssistant:
225				for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
226					if body != "" {
227						body += "\n"
228					}
229					body += "calls " + tc.Name + " " + clipForSummary(tc.Arguments)
230				}
231			}
232			if body == "" {
233				continue
234			}
235			b.WriteString("# " + strings.ToUpper(m.Role) + "\n")
236			b.WriteString(body)
237			b.WriteString("\n")
238		}
239		return b.String()
240	}
241	
242	// clipForSummary caps one tool result or argument blob. The cut is announced so
243	// the model reads a truncated result as truncated rather than as a file that
244	// ends there — the same reason maxToolOutputBytes says so (toolobserve.go).
245	func clipForSummary(s string) string {
246		if len(s) <= summaryToolBytes {
247			return s
248		}
249		return s[:summaryToolBytes] + "\n… (cut; the full result is not part of the summary input)"
250	}
